brief.t: Founded in 1908 in Baroda (Vadodara) by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III; nationalised in 1969.
Government of India owns about 64% of the bank.
Led by MD & CEO Debadatta Chand since 1 July 2023; the government extended his term by three years from July 2026.
FY 2025-26 net profit was ₹20,021 crore, up 2.2%, crossing ₹20,000 crore.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit jumped 35.8% to ₹6,532 crore, its highest-ever quarter; Gross NPA fell to 1.78%.

timeline.t: Founded in Baroda by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III.
Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank merged into BoB, India's first three-way bank merger.

model.how: BoB earns mainly from the interest gap between loans and deposits, plus fees. It also has a large international business and subsidiaries in cards, insurance and asset management.
flow: Customers deposit money in India and abroad
Bank lends to people, farmers, MSMEs and companies

industry.regulator: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Government of India (as main owner)
points: The Government appoints and extends the terms of public sector bank MDs.
BoB has a large overseas network of about 80 branches and offices.
Big theme for interviews: public sector banks now post record profits after cleaning up bad loans.

frameworks.note: Framework views are analysis built from the verified facts on this page, not company statements.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.
glossary.Amalgamation: Two or more companies combining into one. Vijaya Bank and Dena Bank merged into Bank of Baroda in 2019.
glossary.IBPS: Institute of Banking Personnel Selection, which runs common recruitment exams for public sector banks.
glossary.MCLR: Marginal Cost of funds based Lending Rate: the base rate a bank uses to price many loans.

Personality, banking knowledge and HR questions

Finance.q: BoB's Q2 profit rose 35.8% but FY26 profit only 2.2%. Why the difference?
Finance.a: Quarterly profit benefits from loan growth and lower provisions; the full year FY26 was held back by slower interest income growth.

Finance.q: What is Net NPA, and what is BoB's?
Finance.a: Bad loans after money set aside for them. BoB's was 0.37% in Sep 2026.

Marketing.q: How would you market BoB to NRIs?
Marketing.a: Use its overseas branches, easy remittance, NRI deposit products and campaigns in Gulf and UK diaspora communities.

Marketing.q: How would you attract young customers to a 118-year-old bank?
Marketing.a: Combine heritage and trust with a simple app, UPI rewards and student offers.

HR.q: How would you integrate staff after a bank merger?
HR.a: Common training, mixed teams, clear career paths and fair postings. BoB did this after merging Vijaya and Dena.

Sales.q: Sell a BoB home loan to a young salaried couple.
Sales.a: Understand their budget, explain EMI and tenure simply, highlight trust and fast processing, and close with a next step.

Operations.q: How can a public bank cut loan turnaround time?
Operations.a: Digital document collection, automated credit checks and tracking each stage.

Other.q: What do you know about Bank of Baroda?
Other.a: A public sector bank founded in 1908, led by Debadatta Chand, with ₹20,021 cr FY26 profit and a record ₹6,532 cr in Q2 FY27.

gd.t: Were public sector bank mergers a success?

gd.against: Integrating staff and systems took years.

gd.against: Foreign operations bring extra risk and regulation.
